what: X for the B grouping. The frame's X is 'attestations for B, Y, V and U'. The twenty-four filing is a B claim this edition does not itself perform — it ships thirty-nine files — so the edition cannot attest it, and the grouping ledger's own law says only that 'the tradition counts 24' and names nobody. That was the one claim on the door standing on no witness. This record names witnesses on this shelf that state the count, so the door can say who says so.
why_no_quotation: The witness's own words are not copied here. They stand at the address below, in a zone this project holds and hashes; a record that re-types them would be this lane supplying the text, and would carry the witness's license into a file that declares none. The citation is the address. The words are where they were written.

books_24.claim: The books this edition ships as thirty-nine files are counted, in the tradition, as twenty-four.
books_24.not_claimed: That the twenty-four is the text, or older than the thirty-nine, or the division a reader must use. Neither filing is in the ink; this record says only that the count has a witness.

witnesses.reads: Names twenty-four books and identifies them as the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings — the count and the tripartite division in one sentence.
Reports an early codex held in Egypt as having twenty-four books, corrected and pointed by ben Asher and used in Jerusalem to correct other copies.
Rules on the writing of the books by name of the count — the twenty-four standing as a known corpus rather than a proposal.

books_24.how_this_was_found: Every one of the 3,488 zones on this shelf was read and searched for the phrase, contiguously, in the spellings a printer may use. Eleven passages say it; the three above state it about the books rather than in passing. Nothing here is recalled — the search is repeatable against the same bins.
books_24.not_on_this_shelf: The locus usually given for the order of the books, Bava Batra 14b, is in the Babylonian Talmud, which this shelf does not hold. It is deliberately NOT cited: a citation to a record we do not have is the same unattested claim wearing a better label.

binds_to.note: If the grouping ledger is re-issued, this attestation is about the filing that ledger declared and must be re-read against the new one.
